children.text: T1: Sunny

Study the bright circle and dark rings in the photographs below. Idealize the chair leg as a strictly vertical cylinder of radius \(a\), with a smooth, perfectly reflecting surface. You may make additional reasonable simplifying model assumptions and approximations.
a

Find the illuminance surplus \(I(r,\theta)\) inside the bright circle on the floor, for polar radius \(r\gg a\). Illuminance is incoming light per area, and the surplus is the extra illuminance due to the cylinder. Express the result using \(I_0\), the illuminance difference between points A and B in the first photograph.

nodes.alt: Original photograph of sunlight reflected from a vertical chair leg onto the floor, with polar radius r and angle theta measured from the incident-light direction. Nearby points A and B define I0.

children.text: b

Fingers block some light before it reaches the chair leg in the second photograph. Let \(R(\theta)\) be the radial position of the middle dark ring, and \(R_{\min}\) its minimum. Find \(R(\theta)-R_{\min}\).

nodes.alt: Original photograph of a hand blocking sunlight near the chair leg, producing dark rings in the bright reflected patch. The middle-ring radius R(theta) and angle theta are marked.

statement.text:
T1: Sunny
Study the bright circle and dark rings in the photographs below. Idealize the chair leg as a strictly vertical cylinder of radius \(a\), with a smooth, perfectly reflecting surface. You may make additional reasonable simplifying model assumptions and approximations.
a
Find the illuminance surplus \(I(r,\theta)\) inside the bright circle on the floor, for polar radius \(r\gg a\). Illuminance is incoming light per area, and the surplus is the extra illuminance due to the cylinder. Express the result using \(I_0\), the illuminance difference between points A and B in the first photograph.

b
Fingers block some light before it reaches the chair leg in the second photograph. Let \(R(\theta)\) be the radial position of the middle dark ring, and \(R_{\min}\) its minimum. Find \(R(\theta)-R_{\min}\).

children.text: T1: Sunny
a. Reflected illuminance

The nearby A and B readings compare direct sunlight with shadow, so \(I_0\) is the direct-sun illuminance surplus. Let a ray hit the cylinder at a horizontal normal-incidence angle \(\alpha\), and let \(l\) be its horizontal travel distance after reflection. Define \(\beta=\pi-\alpha\). Specular reflection changes the horizontal direction by twice the incidence angle.

nodes.alt: Original top-view ray construction: cylinder radius a, incident transverse coordinate x, reflection angles alpha and beta, polar angle theta, horizontal reflected distance l and floor radius r.
Original side view after rotating the reflected ray into the incident plane: the cylinder centreline, reflection height h, reference height h0, offset a cos(alpha) and distance l are shown.

children.text: An incident strip of width \(dx\) maps into a floor strip of azimuthal width \(2l\,d\alpha\). The vertical-to-floor-distance mapping is the same for the direct and reflected ray, so that factor cancels in power conservation:
\[I_0\,dx=2Il\,d\alpha,\qquad |dx|=a\cos\alpha\,|d\alpha|,\qquad I=\frac{I_0a\cos\alpha}{2l}.\]
To leading order in \(a/r\), \(l\simeq r\) and \(\theta\simeq\pi-2\alpha\). Thus \(\cos\alpha=\sin(\theta/2)\) and
\[I(r,\theta)\simeq\frac{I_0a}{2r}\sin\frac\theta2.\]

Use the full polar angle around the illuminated side, \(0\le\theta\le2\pi\), so the sine is nonnegative. Finite-cylinder corrections are beyond the requested leading far-field approximation. The source also writes the intermediate refinement \(I=-I_0a\cos\beta/\sqrt{4l^2+a^2\sin^2\beta}\), which has the same leading term.
b. Ring position

Approximate the middle blocking finger as horizontal. In the side-view construction the reflected horizontal distance satisfies \(l=l_0+a\cos\alpha\). At grazing incidence \(\alpha=\pi/2\), \(R_{\min}\simeq l_0\). The triangle joining cylinder centre, reflection point and floor point gives
\[r^2=a^2+l^2-2al\cos\beta=a^2+l^2+2al\cos\alpha.\]
Substitute \(l\simeq R_{\min}+a\cos\alpha\) and keep terms through first order in \(a/R_{\min}\). Then \(r^2\simeq R_{\min}^2+4aR_{\min}\cos\alpha\), so
\[R(\theta)-R_{\min}\simeq2a\cos\alpha=2a\sin\frac\theta2.\]

Both the change in the reflected path length and the offset of the reflection point contribute. Dropping either loses the factor of two. The original examiner marking tables remain in the solution PDF.

The source also writes the intermediate refinement \(I=-I_0a\cos\beta/\sqrt{4l^2+a^2\sin^2\beta}\), which has the same leading term.
